text: Recovery Workbench Interface Specifications v4 is issued in Draft status with no approval recorded.
why: This run is the D-RCV-60 realignment: no human approval step is available, the run must not stop for one, and the overlay records the missing status as an assumption.
read: Every interface row, field mapping, outbound check and key row of v4 may be cited by the architecture, requirements and story documents of this run as the interface contract, with Draft status, and the approval is recorded afterwards by the owner of the architecture set.
applied_in: Read me sheet, status line; Interfaces sheet row 3
impact: A service story that cites an interface row cites a document in Draft status until the approval is recorded.

text: INT-19 and INT-20 are removed and the workbook carries 23 numbered interfaces. No replacement reporting interface is written into v4: rwb-reporting builds its read model from events (DP-17, ADR-018) and the interface that delivers that read model is left open.
why: Architecture v5 has no data lake, DP-17 removes both rows and Architecture v5 slide 8 states that the data lake and Power BI are not connected. Writing a new interface row would invent an ID, a system and a payload that no source gives.
read: The two rows are deleted, the description row gives 23 as the count and records 25 for v3, and the Key sheet records the two IDs as removed. The reporting need is carried by rwb-reporting from events into its own read model; the outbound delivery is CG-B-TECH-04-1.
applied_in: Interfaces sheet (rows INT-19 and INT-20 removed, description in row 2); Key sheet (row INT-19, INT-20); Read me sheet (counts and open points); Realignment changes sheet rows 3 and 4
impact: Until the reporting output path is agreed, the reporting story can build the read model but cannot claim a delivered regulatory or Power BI feed, and the COLLINS model-learning feed of INT-20 has no path.

text: An inbound interface stays owned by the ACE team, which ingests the source and runs the checks, and its Recovery-side owning service is rwb-source-data (P1), because only rwb-source-data reads the recovery.v_ace_* views; the business service that consumes the data does so through the P1 contract.
why: ADR-010 and Architecture v5 slide 9 keep the 30 read-only views in the hands of rwb-source-data alone, while version 3 gives the inbound rows the ACE team as owner and no Workbench-side service. The read path of every inbound row is a v_ace_* view, so the owner on the Recovery side can only be the service that reads it.
read: Owner code, Owning service and Owner basis are added as three columns; the Owner column keeps ACE team for the inbound rows and the Owner of the fix column keeps ACE team where it was ACE team. The Field mapping sheet gains the same Owning service column. No existing value of the row is removed or reworded.
applied_in: Interfaces sheet (14 inbound rows and INT-35, INT-36); Field mapping sheet (75 inbound rows)
impact: If a future change lets a service read a view directly, the owning service of that row changes and the ADR-010 decision has to be revisited first.

text: INT-34 (ACE Common) is recorded with P2 rwb-integration as the owning service and the ACE team as the interface owner, because rwb-integration owns the interface configuration and the ACE integration paths; the five capabilities keep the consumers that Architecture v5 slide 30 gives them.
why: The row needs one Recovery-side owner and no source names one. Architecture v5 slide 17 gives rwb-integration the interface config, the file runs, the outbound items and the ACE integration paths, which is the only service whose stated scope covers a shared external contract.
read: Owner stays ACE team; Owner code P2, Owning service P2 rwb-integration and Owner basis cite slide 17 and slide 30. The per-capability consumers of slide 30 are named in the basis and in CG-B-TECH-04-3 so that a later split can be made without research.
applied_in: Interfaces sheet, row INT-34; Field mapping sheet (no row); Read me sheet open points
impact: If INT-34 splits per capability, four more rows appear with rwb-access, rwb-case, rwb-treatment and rwb-comms as owners and the P2 row shrinks to the contract itself.

text: INT-14 (WIN registered mail) is owned by P6 rwb-comms, which owns the notice and the 16:00 window, and the file is built and transferred by P2 rwb-integration as an activity of the interface run.
why: Version 3 names the single Workbench, which no longer exists as an owner; Architecture v5 slide 17 names rwb-integration; the Ownership Map ruling for JOB-10 splits the two, and the Service Catalog v1 gives rwb-comms the WIN letters handed to rwb-integration.
read: Owner becomes P6 rwb-comms, Owner code P6, Owning service P6 rwb-comms, and Owner of the fix becomes 'P6 rwb-comms; P2 rwb-integration for the file transfer'. Retry and acknowledgement stay as version 3 writes them.
applied_in: Interfaces sheet, row INT-14; Field mapping sheet, four INT-14 rows
impact: If rwb-integration is named the owner instead, the notice content and the 16:00 window have no owner and the JOB-10 ruling has to be reopened.

text: INT-25 (debt-buyer data tape) is owned by S6 rwb-debtsale, which owns the lot and the account set, and the encrypted file and its manifest are built and transferred by P2 rwb-integration.
why: Version 3 names the single Workbench, which no longer exists as an owner; Architecture v5 slide 17 names rwb-integration for the transfer; the Service Catalog v1 gives the S6 file contract as the buyer file per lot through rwb-integration.
read: Owner becomes S6 rwb-debtsale, Owner code S6, Owning service S6 rwb-debtsale, and Owner of the fix becomes 'S6 rwb-debtsale; P2 rwb-integration for the file transfer'. The personal-data rule of the sale terms stays as the row writes it.
applied_in: Interfaces sheet, row INT-25; Field mapping sheet, three INT-25 rows
impact: If rwb-integration is named the owner instead, the content of the tape and the sale terms have no owning service and the personal-data rule loses its point of control.

text: INT-24 (partner portal) is owned by S9 rwb-partner and read as the partner gateway interface with FAPI 2.0 in front of rwb-partner, keeping OpenAPI 3.1 as its standard; the partner and agency manager stays named after the service as party of the fix.
why: Architecture v5 slide 8 says the partner gateway fronts rwb-partner and v3 names the single Workbench, which no longer exists as an owner; the results that partners report are rwb-partner events under the Ownership Map ruling for EV-21.
read: Owner becomes S9 rwb-partner, Owner code S9, Owning service S9 rwb-partner, and Owner of the fix becomes 'S9 rwb-partner; partner and agency manager'. The screen wording of the Approach column is kept; the interface is read through the partner gateway.
impact: If the interface is screen-based instead, the partner gateway and FAPI 2.0 drop out and the partner access rule has to be rewritten.

text: INT-21 is owned by P4 rwb-access, and the group-to-role mapping reaches rwb-access through the rwb-source-data contract, which is the only reader of v_ace_iam_group, and is cached by rwb-access for the sign-in check.
why: Architecture v5 slide 30 (1) puts the Recovery roles, scope, masking and DoA in rwb-access while ADR-010 keeps the v_ace_* views with rwb-source-data; the two rules together force the mapping through the P1 contract, and no source states it in words.
read: Owner stays ACE team; Owner code P4, Owning service P4 rwb-access and Owner of the fix 'P4 rwb-access; ACE team for the sign-in'. The read of the mapping is recorded as a P1 contract plus an rwb-access cache.
impact: If rwb-access reads the view directly, ADR-010 has to be amended and every other service gains the same permission.

text: INT-22 (PII Kafka, audit and SOC logs) is owned by the platform observability set RWB-PLT-OBS, because every one of the 19 services sends audit and personal-data access logs and no single business service can own the sender; the ACE team stays the owner of the interface and of the SOC path.
why: Architecture v5 slide 30 (2) gives the consumer as all 19 services, so the only single owner is the platform capability that ships the library; Architecture v5 slide 23 keeps the PII topics separate from the Recovery business-event topics.
read: Owner stays ACE team; Owner code PLT, Owning service 'platform observability (RWB-PLT-OBS)' and Owner of the fix 'PLT (RWB-PLT-OBS); ACE team for the PII Kafka path'. The topic, schema and library are left open in CG-B-TECH-04-7.
impact: If a business service is named instead, the other 18 services have no owner of the sender and each one writes its own client.

text: INT-35 and INT-36 are owned on the Recovery side by P1 rwb-source-data as the reader of v_ace_credit_decision and v_ace_esign, with rwb-treatment as the consumer of the credit decision and rwb-document as the consumer of the e-signature status; INT-23 (Enterprise AI) is owned by P10 rwb-agent.
why: ADR-010 keeps every recovery.v_ace_* read with rwb-source-data, Architecture v5 slide 30 (4) puts the restructure calculator call in rwb-treatment, the Ownership Map ruling puts signature_request in rwb-document, and Architecture v5 slides 6 and 8 give the Enterprise AI endpoint to rwb-agent.
read: Owner stays ACE team for INT-35 and INT-36 and Bank platform for INT-23; the Owner code column gives P1, P1 and P10, and the Owner of the fix column names the service first. The consumer services are recorded in the basis and in CG-B-TECH-04-9.
applied_in: Interfaces sheet, rows INT-23, INT-35 and INT-36
impact: If the consumer is named as the owner instead, the view read moves away from rwb-source-data and ADR-010 has to be amended.

text: The two citations of Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v7 in the Field mapping description and the Key sheet are kept unchanged in v4 and recorded as a documentation gap.
why: The rule of this run is to keep every value of the source and to change only what the realignment needs; the field IDs DF-XXX-nnn do not change between v7 and v8, and repointing a citation is a documentation edit for the owner of the LDM.
read: The 82 field mappings keep their DF-* IDs and are read as compatible with the latest LDM; the citation is corrected when the next LDM is issued.
applied_in: Field mapping sheet, row 2 description; Key sheet, row 'LDM field'
impact: A reader of v4 is pointed at an older LDM version; no mapping row is affected.

text: No release date appears in the source workbook, so v4 adds none; the change-log row carries 22 November 2026, and any release date written into the workbook later is tentative.
why: The source Interface Specifications v3 carries no release date on any sheet, and the run fixes dates as unchanged and tentative (U7) with no date raised as a gap.
read: A reader takes the interface set as applying to waves 1 to 4 of the Ownership Map v1, with the dates of the programme plan and marked tentative when they appear.
applied_in: Read me sheet, release line and change log; Realignment changes sheet row 12
impact: None on the interface content; a plan that needs a date takes it from the programme plan.
